facility.name: Lil' Munchkins Child Care Center
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Drop-In Care,Part Time Care,Transportation to/from School

provenance.note: Census Geocoder Exact match: 4106 SAN PEDRO AVE, SAN ANTONIO, TX, 78212

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: Three out of four files evaluated did not have Handling Hazardous Materials training available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Franchise Tax Delinquent: According to the Texas Comptroller website, the business entity's Franchise Tax Account Status is Inactive/Forfeited. The operation is currently providing care to children with an inactive status.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Franchise Tax Delinquent (26 TAC §745.247)

occurrences.finding: Report Number of Employees: The operation did not report the number of employees who left from the prior year by 01/15/26.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: At time of inspection, infant class had five children to one caregiver, specified age group was eleven months. Class was out of ratio by one child.     This was corrected at inspection as a second caregiver was placed in the class.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: At time of inspection, cleaning solutions were observed at children's reach.     At time of inspection, diaper creams were observed in children's reach.     At time of inspection, a potty chair was observed to not be sanitized.     This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: The Twos room had 12 children with one caregiver. The specified age group was two. This was corrected at inspection when a child was moved to another room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on the DFPS investigation, a caregiver exercised poor judgment when the caregiver, at the time of transportation pick up, did not verify with either the parent or school whether a child went home sick from school that day.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: Based on the DFPS investigation, the operation did not complete an accident report for a child who was left unsupervised in a transportation van within 48 hours of the incident occurring.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS Investigation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: Based on the DFPS investigation, the operation failed to notify Child Care Regulation within the required 48 hours of a child being left unsupervised in a transportation van.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - Driver or designated employee conduct walk-through and visual check of vehicle: Based on the DFPS investigation and observation of the caregiver re-enacting transportation procedures, it was determined the caregiver did not walk to the back of the van to ensure there were no children in the last seat.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - Driver or designated employee conduct walk-through and visual check of vehicle (26 TAC §746.5625(d)(2))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: The director was aware of a child being left unsupervised in a transportation van and chose not to report the incident to Child Care Regulation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - Account for All Children: Based on the DFPS investigation, the caregiver did not account for all the children in the transportation van prior to exiting the vehicle.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - Account for All Children (26 TAC §746.5605(3))

occurrences.finding: AP Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - No Child Unattended: Based on the DFPS investigation, a child was left unsupervised in a locked van for 2 hours.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Safety Precautions for Loading and Unloading Children - No Child Unattended (26 TAC §746.5605(4))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric CPR: Two of ten staff files audited did not have CPR training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(4)(A))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985): Two of ten staff files audited did not have affidavits on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985) (26 TAC §746.901(4))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing: Two of ten staff files audited did not have first aid training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(3)(A))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: A wall in the Pre-K room had peeling paint and exposed drywall.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements: One of ten staff files audited did not have proof of educational requirements.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements (26 TAC §746.901(2))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: The Pre-K class had 20 children, whose ages ranged from three to four years, with one caregiver. The specified age group was four. This was corrected at inspection when a second caregiver came into the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Infant Daily Report - Share with Parent: Infant daily reports were not being provided in a written or electronic format.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Daily Report - Share with Parent (26 TAC §746.2431)

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: Seven of seven staff had expired first aid certificates.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: No Swaddling of Infant Unless Completed Sleep Exception Form on File: An infant was asleep in a crib while swaddled. This was corrected when the caregiver removed the child from the swaddle.
occurrences.violation_type_title: No Swaddling of Infant Unless Completed Sleep Exception Form on File (26 TAC §746.2428)

occurrences.finding: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization: A child who was injured was taken to the hospital for treatment and Child Care Regulation was not notified.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Emergency Evacuation and Relocation Diagram - Posted in Each Room: Evacuation and relocation diagrams were not posted in each classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Emergency Evacuation and Relocation Diagram - Posted in Each Room (26 TAC §746.5207(b))

occurrences.finding: Measurement of Use Zone for Swings - in Front and Rear: A new swing set was installed. The center beam height is over eight feet. The rear use zone is 14 feet. The children will not use the swings until  this deficiency is corrected.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Measurement of Use Zone for Swings - in Front and Rear (26 TAC §746.4807(a))

occurrences.finding: Fenced Outdoor Activity Space -Gates Locked: The outside exit to the playground was locked from the outside. This was corrected at inspection when the lock was turned to be accessed from inside the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fenced Outdoor Activity Space -Gates Locked (26 TAC §746.4309)

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less: A piece of climbing equipment with a height of 24 inches was placed over grass.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less (26 TAC §746.4907(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Arrangement of Napping Equipment -Provides Sufficient Walking and Work Space: A classroom was observed to be have cots tightly placed with no aisles for a walk or work space.  This was corrected at inspection when a discussion was had about cot placement.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Arrangement of Napping Equipment -Provides Sufficient Walking and Work Space (26 TAC §746.2909(3))

occurrences.finding: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance: Based on the information gathered, caregivers did not use positive methods of discipline and guidance when redirecting children and putting them in time out.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance (26 TAC §746.2803(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: Based off the DFPS investigation, several children stated that a caregiver would yell at them at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based off of the DFPS investigation, children cleaned tables using chemicals while in care at the operation. And, based off of the DFPS investigation, a caregiver provided a personal tablet to children with a pixelated video of nude people.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based off the DFPS investigation a caregiver fell asleep while directly supervising children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: Based off of the DFPS investigation, a caregiver was found reason to believe for sexual abuse. A child made an outcry of being inappropriately touched by the caregiver while in care at the center.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Written Operational Policies - Promotion of Physical Activity: A statement promoting active play was not present in the operational policies.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Promotion of Physical Activity (26 TAC §746.501(a)(18))

occurrences.finding: Posting Requirements - List entitled "Current Employees"--sized at least 81/2 X 11 inches, printed legibly, include employee first and last name: A current employee list was not posted. This was corrected at inspection when a new list was posted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Posting Requirements - List entitled "Current Employees"--sized at least 81/2 X 11 inches, printed legibly, include employee first and last name (26 TAC §746.401(9))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact: Nine of ten children's files did not have addresses listed for the emergency contacts.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact (26 TAC §746.605(6))

occurrences.finding: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually: It was determined through the course of the investigation that a caregiver transported children without having taken the transportation safety training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually (26 TAC §746.1316(a))

occurrences.finding: First Aid Kit - Incomplete Kit: There were scissors and a thermometer missing from the first aid kit located in the vehicle to transport children.     Note: There was a staff member that grabbed a thermometer and scissors from the operation and put them in the vehicle's first aid kit to make it complete.
occurrences.violation_type_title: First Aid Kit - Incomplete Kit (26 TAC §746.4003(a))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: A classroom was observed to be out of ratio when a group of children with a specified age group of 0-11 months old was observed to have 6 children with one caregiver. The maximum number of children allowed for one caregiver for this age group is 4 children.     Note: The director entered the classroom to be counted in ratio.     A classroom was observed to be out of ratio when a group of children with a specified age group of 3 years old was observed to have 22 children with one caregiver. The maximum number of children allowed for one caregiver would be 15 children for this age group.     Note: There were some parents that picked up their children to make the classroom in ratio.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Maximum Group Size 13 or More Children: A classroom was observed to be out of ratio when a group of children with a specified age group of 12-18 months was observed to have 15 children with two caregivers.  The maximum group size for two or more caregivers for this specified age group is two caregivers to 12 children.     Note: This was corrected when 3 children were moved to another classroom making the classroom in ratio.    A classroom was observed to be out of ratio when a group of children with a specified age group of 5 to 12 years old was observed to have 40 children with two caregivers.  The maximum group size for two or more caregivers for this specified age group is two caregivers to 35 children.     Note: Parents were picking up children and 5 children were picked up making the classroom in ratio.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maximum Group Size 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1609)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired: There was a piece of playground equipment was cracked and broken. Additionally there was metal pieces from a fence that were found on the grass area on the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired (26 TAC §746.4751(c))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Entanglement Protrusions or Openings: There was a strand of barbed wire that was on the operation's side of the fence. The barbed wire is sharp and rusty.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Entanglement Protrusions or Openings (26 TAC §746.4601(4))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Entrapment Openings: There was a fence located towards the backside of the playground, that was leaning over. With the fence leaning over it created a huge gap/opening.     Additionally there were some rusty wires that were trying to hold the fence in place, but with it leaning the wires were exposed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Entrapment Openings (26 TAC §746.4601(3))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: There was a wall located in the hallway next to the restrooms, that had a hole towards the bottom of the wall.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: A classroom was observed to be out of ratio when a group of children with a specified age group of 5 years old was observed to have 24 children with one caregiver.  The caregiver to child ratio for this specified age group for one teacher is 22 children.  The operation corrected this at inspection when an afternoon caregiver arrived to make the clasrsroom in ratio.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Maximum Group Size 13 or More Children: A classroom was observed to be out of ratio when a group of children with a specified age group of 0-11 months old was observed to have 12 children with two caregivers.  The caregiver to child ratio for this specified age group for two teachers is 10 children.    The operation corrected this when two children were  picked up for the day making the classroom compliant.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maximum Group Size 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1609)

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: A classroom was observed to be out of ratio when a group of children with a specified age group of 3 years old was observed to have 27 children with one caregiver.  The caregiver to child ratio for this specified age group for one teacher is 15 children.    The operation corrected this at inspection when the caregiver that immediately returned on bus run was added to ratio making the classroom compliant.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: There was a disinfectant solution underneath a sink in the school age classroom. Also in all the bathrooms there was a plunger,toilet scrub brush accessible to children, and trash cans without lids.       Note: This was corrected at inspection when the operation's director removed all toilet scrub brushes, plungers, cleaning supplies, and trash cans from all the restrooms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit: There were five employee files that were viewed. There were three employee files that did not have a notarized affidavit available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985) (26 TAC §746.901(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Medical Authorization: There were two out of the five children files viewed that did not have their authorization for medical treatment completed in their enrollment paperwork.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Special Needs Statement (26 TAC §746.605(12))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Label for Each Infant: None of the cribs in the infant room where labeled with each child's name.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Label for Each Infant (26 TAC §746.2409(a)(10))

occurrences.finding: First Aid Kit - Incomplete Kit: The first aid kit was missing twizzers to make the kit complete.
occurrences.violation_type_title: First Aid Kit - Incomplete Kit (26 TAC §746.4003(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Date of Admission: There were four out of the five children records that were missing their admission date.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Date of Admission (26 TAC §746.605(3))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact: There were two out of the five children records that did not have the address of an emergency contact.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact (26 TAC §746.605(6))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Entrapment Openings: There was a gap of more than 4 inches where the fence did not meet the pavement on the toddler outdoor play area.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Entrapment Openings (26 TAC §746.4601(3))

occurrences.finding: Signed Admission Form: There were two out of the five children files that did not have a parent signature on the enrollment forms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Signed Admission Form (26 TAC §746.607)

occurrences.finding: Director Annual Training 30 Hours Required: The center director did not have the annual 30 hours of completed training available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Annual Training 30 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1311(a))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: There were no updated infant feeding schedules for this month, available upon review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current: There were two children files out of the five children files viewed that did not have updated immunization records available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current (26 TAC §746.613(b))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required: There were four out of the five employee files that did not have 24 hours of annual training available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1309(a))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: There was not an updated fire inspection that was completed for the current year. The last inspection was completed on 9/22/2020.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))
